data.narrative:
Perennial Autonomy is a government-contract-stage defense and security company backed by Schmidt and staffed with talent from SpaceX, Google, and Apple. The target has secured $500M in IDIQ funding and prior private capital. The Defense & Security sector comprises 26 known peers, including 2 public comparables (DRSHF, IDEAFORGE.NS) and 8 private firms such as Anduril Industries, Helsing, Castelion, Shield AI, and Saronic.

Peer-median valuation proved inapplicable due to insufficient narrow-stage comparables. No same-stage, adjacent-stage, or similar-valuation-tier peers existed in sufficient quantity (minimum 3 required) to produce a reliable median. While 26 total Defense & Security peers exist, none met the filtering criteria for defensible triangulation. Relying on all-sector medians would introduce unacceptable sector-specific distortion given government contracting's distinct dynamics, risk profile, and revenue recognition patterns.

Without robust peer triangulation, this analysis cannot currently support a specific valuation range. Resolution requires either: (i) deeper diligence into the top five private peers to establish post-money valuations at comparable rounds, (ii) revenue and margin data from public Defense & Security comparables to anchor DCF assumptions, or (iii) disclosed terms from recent IDIQ-backed fundings. The $500M contract provides revenue visibility but does not itself imply enterprise value absent contract margins, working capital, and capital intensity. Key uncertainties include government customer concentration risk and the transferability of tech-team domain expertise into government procurement execution.
